name: Royal Coachman
imitates: The classic flashy attractor, tied here as a feather-wing wet fly. The red band and white wings stand out underwater, and it works as a searching fly or dropper when nothing is hatching.
recipe: Peacock herl, red floss and peacock herl in even thirds
White goose shoulder or covert, or swan

steps.text: Attach the black thread and tie in a golden pheasant tippet tail the full length of the hook shank.
Tie in peacock herl the full length of the shank.
Wrap the herl over the back third of the shank and tie off, but do not cut it. Leave room at the front for the hackle and wing.
Tie in red floss and bind it down over the middle third, together with the remaining herl.
Wrap the red floss over the middle third, tie off and cut off the waste.
Wrap the remaining peacock herl over the forward third of the shank.
Stroke back the fibres on a natural brown hackle, cut off the tip leaving a small triangle, and tie it in directly in front of the herl.
Wrap the hackle two or three turns and tie off.
With the thread, gather the hackle fibres to the sides and below the shank to form a false hackle.
Cut two matching slips of white feather for the wings, one from each of a left and a right feather.
Tie the wings down on top of the hook, supporting them between your fingers as the thread compresses them. If they slip, unwind and try again.
